newsitem.title: USA: Waste Management to sell Wessex Water stake.
newsitem.headline: Waste Management to sell Wessex Water stake.

text.p: Waste Management International Plc, a British-based subsidiary of WMX Technologies, Inc., has agreed to sell its 19.5 percent equity investment in water utility Wessex Water Plc, the companies said Wednesday
Total after-tax proceeds are expected to be about $259 million in cash, WMX said.
Under the agreement, Waste Management will sell about 87 percent of the 19.5 percent stake it bought in 1991 to Wessex, and divest the remaining 13 percent in open market stock sales.
Waste Management had previously agreed not to sell its interest in Wessex until early 1998.
WMX said the sale will result in a fourth-quarter after-tax charge of about $88 million, or 18 cents per share, and reduce 1997 earnings by 4 cents per share.

"The agreement with Wessex represents another important step in our plans to simplify our organisational structure, narrow our scope of activities and enhance shareholder value," said Phillip Rooney, president and chief executive of WMX.
Oak Brook, Ill.-based WMX said Waste Management will use proceeds from the sale to reduce debt and focus more capital on its core waste services business.
Including the Wessex deal, WMX has generated nearly $1 billion in cash from the sale of non-core and underperforming assets, a target it established last May.
WMX said it plans additional asset sales, including other noncore equity investments, real estate and underperforming core businesses.

WMX said the ownership structure of Wessex Waste Management Ltd, the waste services joint venture between Wessex Water and Waste Management International, will remain unchanged. The joint venture operates UK Waste Ltd., one of Britain's largest waste services companies.
Separately, Wessex announced a package of share buybacks, making good on a pledge to deliver higher returns to shareholders after a recent bid for South West Water was frustrated.

Wessex, sitting on a healthy cash pile, said it would offer to buy back up to 10 percent of its ordinary shares at 380 pence ($6.33) each in an attempt to simplify its capital structure and increase earnings and dividends.
WMX's stock rose 50 cents to $33.50 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
